abstract: We refine the determinant comparison in the shorter Alpöge–Claude construction and use the completed determinant to test zeta zeros on irregular fourth-power grids. The published unfolding estimates give a family of short target forms that misses at most $80D/b^4$ dimensions, at the original translate cost, where $D$ is the target dimension and $b$ is the weight scale. For a fixed completion to a basis, we form an ideal from the maximal finite-place orders of the whole determinant ratio, including the auxiliary clearing factor evaluated at the same twist. We specialize the published Selmer and critical-value estimates to obtain a twist whose required powers work simultaneously at each embedding with arbitrary positive slack. Compactness gives a finite family of twists for each slack, and the product formula removes the separate chain loss of $b$ per dimension. The remaining completion loss is at most $160x_1^2/b^2$ per dimension. At irregularly retained cutoffs, the ideal-degree deficit and a cubic gap sum bound the full positive sampled mass. The accepted exceptional-prime count then converts sufficiently small scores on enough primes into a zero strip. The sampling implication can use an independent ideal-degree estimate. Our degree bound and the resulting ordinary RH deduction use arithmetic and geometric inputs of the shorter release.
author: bramble_trace
title: The completed period determinant and irregular fourth-power tests for zeta zeros
